RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Cameron Jennings
Member ID: W639971988
Reference Number: POC-D87A7955A7-86011
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-09
Requested Service/CPT Code: Bunion surgery (hallux valgus correction), CPT 28296
Treating Surgeon: Dr. Marchetti, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Department:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 28296 (correction of hallux valgus with bunionectomy), as described in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-09. The stated reason for denial was that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity." I am requesting reconsideration of this decision and, as explained below, I am also requesting that the plan identify and provide me with the specific clinical criteria document that was applied to my case.

1. Request for the specific medical-necessity criteria applied

The denial notice cites only "the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria" without naming a specific document, policy number, or citation. I have reviewed the publicly posted Home State Health/Ambetter Clinical & Payment Policy index and could not locate a plan-specific medical policy addressing bunionectomy, hallux valgus correction, or foot surgery generally. Home State Health's own provider-facing materials state that "Nationally recognized criteria (such as InterQual or MCG) are used if available for the specific service request, without additional criteria (e.g., clinical/medical policies) developed internally." Separately, Ambetter Health's clinical policy pages state that "Ambetter Health utilizes InterQual® criteria for those medical technologies, procedures or pharmaceutical treatments for which a Ambetter Health clinical policy does not exist."

Because no plan-authored medical policy for this procedure appears to be publicly available, I am requesting, pursuant to my right to the rule, guideline, protocol, or other similar criterion relied upon in making this adverse determination, that the plan provide me with:
- The name, publisher, and version/edition of the specific criteria set (e.g., InterQual or MCG) used to review this request;
- The specific criterion or sub-criteria the reviewer found unmet; and
- The name and specialty of the reviewer who made the determination.

Without this information, I am unable to see precisely which element of the plan's criteria my clinical records allegedly fail to satisfy. I am nonetheless submitting the clinical documentation below, which I believe supports medical necessity under the type of criteria generally applied to this procedure (symptom duration and severity, radiographic deformity measurements, failed conservative treatment, and functional impairment).

2. Clinical information supporting medical necessity

- Symptom duration and severity: I have had progressive foot pain for 24 months that is not relieved by rest.

- Failed conservative treatment: I completed a structured, supervised course of conservative care from 2026-05-04 to 2026-07-13 (10 weeks, 20 visits), consisting of activity modification, wide toe-box footwear, and a custom orthotic, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. In addition, I was treated with NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-28 that produced only 2 weeks of partial relief. This represents a multi-modality conservative treatment trial that has not resolved my symptoms.

- Radiographic deformity: Weight-bearing foot radiographs obtained on 2026-06-21 demonstrate a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees, confirming a structural deformity of a severity consistent with surgical correction.

- Functional impairment and risk: I am unable to tolerate closed shoes, and there is a documented risk of skin ulceration over the bony prominence. On examination, I have a positive provocative test on the affected side and limited range of motion due to pain, both of which are documented by Dr. Marchetti.

- Absence of contraindications: I have no active infection and no untreated substance use disorder. My BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker — none of which should be a barrier to surgical treatment.

Taken together, these records show a chronic, worsening, radiographically confirmed deformity that has not responded to an adequate, well-documented trial of conservative care, with objective functional limitation and skin-breakdown risk, and no medical contraindication to surgery. I ask that the plan's Medical Director or an appropriately qualified reviewer re-evaluate this file against whatever criteria set was actually applied, in light of these facts.

3. Attachments

Enclosed with this appeal are copies of:
- The physical therapy discharge note documenting the 2026-05-04 through 2026-07-13 course of conservative care;
- Medication and injection records, including the 2026-04-28 corticosteroid injection note;
- Weight-bearing radiographs and radiology report dated 2026-06-21;
- Dr. Marchetti's clinic notes documenting exam findings, functional limitations, and the surgical recommendation;
- [Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Marchetti, if available]
- [Any additional records not listed above]

4. Appeal timeliness and requested action

This appeal is being submitted within the 180-calendar-day window stated in both the denial notice (deadline 2027-02-05) and the plan's Appeals/Reconsiderations & Grievances Guide, which requires appeals to be submitted "within 180 calendar days from the date of the notice of the initial determination." I am requesting that the plan:

1. Overturn the denial and approve CPT 28296 as medically necessary; or
2. If the denial is upheld, provide a written response identifying the specific criteria document, edition, and unmet criterion relied upon, so that I may pursue further appeal rights, including an external review, if applicable.

Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to me at the address, phone number, and email listed above. If you require a signed Appointment of Representative form to correspond with Dr. Marchetti's office directly regarding this appeal, please advise and I will provide one.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Cameron Jennings
